text: Hello everybody.Nice to see you again.Welcome to my English class.Please get your students book and the worksheet ready.Let's start today's lesson with a revision.I wonder if you still remember this picture.Which poem does it go with?Never a dull moment.Do you remember who's who in the picture?Who is the boy standing in the middle?He's the speaker of the poem.Who is the old man slamming the door?He's the speaker's grandpa.Who is the screaming little girl?The speaker's sister.And who is the man singing in the bathtub?He is the speaker's dad.Remember my questions?There are all questions with the word who.Who is a pronoun and interrogative pronoun.We can use who to ask about persons.Here are some example sentences using the pronoun who.Who wrote the poem Never a dull moment?Who has written a poem in English before?When we talk about family members, we can use the pronoun who.Now you can see a family tree of the Lee family.Can you tell me who they are?Who is Robert?His child's father, right?The word he is used to refer to Robert.And who's Stella?She's Jennifer's daughter.Who's Helen?She's Tommy's aunt.Who's Kenny?He's Helen's husband and George's father.Now can you use the same pattern to make dialogues?Time is up.Let's look at the samples.Who is Jennifer?She's Paul's wife.And she's also Tommy and Stella's mother.By the way, we add the apostrophe and S to the second person only.Because Tommy and Stella share the same mother.Who is Anne?She's Charles and Alice's daughter.We can also say she is Paul and Helen's sister.And you may have other answers.Look at the family tree.Can you complete this sentence?Here is the answer.So, whose father is Kenny?George's.George's father is Kenny.Whose is the possessive of who.We can use whose followed by a noun to ask who owns something or has something.That means the word whose is about possession.Here are some example sentences using the pronoun whose.Whose photos are these?They are my photos.Whose mother is Helen?George's mother is Helen.In these two examples, whose is followed by a noun, photos and mother.When describing the family relationship, we can use whose as well.Let's ask and answer questions about the family tree using whose.She's George's mother.Here she refers to Helen.Now use the sentence patterns to make dialogues.Here are the sample dialogues for you.Two more dialogues to practice.Don't forget to use whose as well as the words in the blue box.These samples are for your reference.Whose aunt is Helen?Tommy and Stella's.She's Tommy and Stella's aunt.Whose cousin is Tommy?He's George's cousin.Good.So far we've used whose followed by a noun to ask about the relationship or ownership.Actually, we can also use whose not followed by a noun.Look at the examples.Instead of asking whose chopsticks are those, we can also say whose are those chopsticks.The two questions share the same meaning, no difference in fact.A practice for you.Use the pictures to ask and answer questions.Remember, use whose not followed by a noun.Sam and Sophie, would you please show us the dialogues?Whose is this pair of glasses?It's James.Whose is this watch?It's Wendy's.Whose are these books?They're Andrew's.Thank you guys.And what about you?Did you use the correct language?So far, I suppose you've heard whose a lot of times.Hang on a moment here.I'd like to talk about these two words.They sound the same, don't they?Whose.But they're spelled differently and have different meanings.Because they sound alike, they're often confused.Let's get into the difference between whose and whose.Whose is a contraction, which means it's two words stuck together.It can mean who is or who has.For example, who's hungry means who is hungry.Who's got the answer means who has got the answer.As I said earlier, whose is the possessive of who.In the sentence, I wonder whose books they are.Whose is used to ask who owns the books.So, who's got clear about the difference between whose and whose?Hopefully, all of you.Now I've got some questions for you.Grab your pen, complete the questions with whose or whose.This is task one on your worksheet.Have you finished?Let's check the answers.Whose younger sister is she?Who's going to Eva's party?It means who is going to Eva's party.Who's already finished the task?Who's here is the contraction of who has.Who has already finished the task?And whose mobile phone should I use?Wait a second.If someone asks you whose mobile phone should I use?And you're willing to offer your phone, what would you say?Probably you can use my mobile phone.To make the answer shorter and simpler, you can say, you can use mine.The word mine is a possessive adjective, as you already learned in unit five.The word mine is a possessive pronoun.We often use a possessive pronoun when we know what noun we are talking about and we don't want to repeat it.Like in the mobile phone sentence, the speaker uses mine instead of saying mobile phone again.In addition to my, there are other possessive adjectives like these.And the possessive pronouns are these.Is there anything missing here?Yes, its is not here.We don't use its as a possessive pronoun.Think about the part of speech of my, yours, his, her, our, and their.They are possessive adjectives, right?They function as adjectives.Like other adjectives, they are used to describe nouns like the mobile phone in the example sentence.So possessive adjectives must have nouns after them.What is the part of speech of mine, yours, his, etc.? They are possessive pronouns.They are used instead of the nouns.So they stand alone with no nouns after them.Here is task two.Write the correct possessive pronouns for the underlying words.The first one has been done for you.Please do it on your worksheet.Thank you for watching.Have you finished the task?It's time to check the answers.Number two, my name can be replaced by mine.Number three, your first name can be yours.Number four, his middle name can be his.Number five, we can use hers instead of her last name.Number six, we can say theirs and the last one, our children can be replaced by ours, clear?Now let's practice more.Members of the Li family are doing different jobs, and these are the things they use for them.Have a look.But whose are they?Whose dictionary is this?What would
